title: Crown and Oath
premise: Odile Okafor, a cartographer who once mapped the unmapped realms before magic was outlawed, has hidden for seven years among the charm-sellers of Greyhallow City. When the old gods suddenly begin answering prayers again — wild, desperate, and unbound — Odile's dormant gift awakens, and they discover their own blood carries the covenant that once bound gods and mortals together. Hunted by the city's god-hunters and courted by fractious deities, Odile must gather a found family of outcasts to reforge the broken covenant at the Worldspine. In the end, Odile chooses neither god nor mortal but a third oath of their own making, sealing the realms together at the cost of their maps, their anonymity, and the life they built.
about_author: August Yarrow is the pen name of a former field cartographer who traded surveying instruments for folklore archives across three continents. They write fantasy about people who belong everywhere and nowhere, and they still cannot resist drawing a map in the margins of every manuscript.

chapters.title: The First Answered Prayer
chapters.summary: Odile Okafor's POV. In outlawed-magic Greyhallow, Odile sells harmless charms by day and hides their cartographer's gift by night. When a dying child's prayer is answered by a forgotten river god manifesting in the market square, Odile's old maps ignite with light — and so does their blood. The god names them heir to the covenant. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant wonder as a buried identity resurfaces.

chapters.title: A Company of the Unwanted
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, with interludes from ex-god-hunter Sefa Vane. Fleeing the Wardens, Odile assembles a ragged family: Sefa, who defected rather than burn a god-child; Bramble, a half-fae scribe; and the river god Weyl, diminished and bitter. Together they decode the covenant's terms — it requires blood-heir, witness, and willing god at the Worldspine before the solstice. Emotional beat: guarded strangers becoming something like kin.

chapters.title: The Solstice Road
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The journey to the Worldspine becomes a gauntlet: Weyl is captured by rival gods demanding the covenant name them supreme, Sefa's former order closes in, and Odile learns the original covenant demanded an heir's death. Betrayed by exhaustion and fear, Odile nearly abandons the quest — until their found family refuses to leave without them. Emotional beat: despair breaking open into chosen loyalty; the climax begins as they storm the godhold to free Weyl.

chapters.title: A Third Oath
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the Worldspine on solstice night, Odile faces the assembled gods and the covenant's cruel original terms. Refusing both sacrifice and supremacy, they draft a new covenant in living ink — binding realms through mutual obligation rather than blood — with Sefa as witness and a freed, willing Weyl as signatory. Magic returns lawfully; Greyhallow's ban shatters. Emotional beat: hard-won belonging; Odile ends not hidden, but home.
